requirement: Annex K defines a carrier-sense, collision-avoiding way for STANAG 5066 nodes to share one frequency.
CSMA adds no D_PDU types and needs no explicit peer-to-peer exchange; access decisions rest only on the node's local view of channel activity and what it infers about other nodes.
For CSMA to work, the options chosen and the timer values must be set the same on every node of the network.
notes: Text says they 'need to be set consistently'; K.5, p.K-13 says Annex K requires it. Mode and timers are documented as network-wide settings (plan 7.2, D7).

requirement: Annex K is Optional in the standard, but our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency makes it mandatory.
Any CSMA or other listen-before-transmit mechanism used with STANAG 5066 must conform to Annex K.
notes: Covers our optional external busy input (K-0006) and identification hook transmissions (K-0007).

requirement: External busy input: Annex K considers only DCD and VDCD; other users of the channel are NOT STATED. Reading: the optional external busy signal (off by default) is ORed into Annex K's DCD input, so it is listen-before-transmit that conforms to Annex K and can only make the node more cautious. An idle decision that it delays counts as DCD-determined.

Identification hook output (decision D4) is a transmission of its own, queued like data and sent only through the Annex K states; it is never put inside a 5066 transmission and never sent before another node's EOT end time.
notes: Plan 4.4 identification row, 9.1; Ed4 C.7.5.4.3, p.C-114.

requirement: Ed4 adds new timer values for better performance on networks with few nodes; the differences from Ed3 are listed in K.5.
The Ed3 protocol used a jitter mechanism (from a 2002 HFIA presentation) so that many nodes could reduce the chance of collision.
Ed4 addition 1: an optional slotted mechanism with a slot per node, for faster switching and more resilience in small networks; jitter remains an option for larger networks.
Ed4 addition 2: optimised switching when only two nodes are communicating.
notes: K.2.6; K.3.2.2 rule 1. K.2.1 says this leaves no remaining reason to run without CSMA or WTRP, and that Annex K should outperform WTRP on lightly loaded networks [p.K-2]; compare J-0068.

requirement: Ed4 addition 3: different timings when a STANAG 5066 EOT is detected, for faster switching than one timer allows.
Ed4 addition 4: better handling of a node sending several transmissions in a row, important for non-ARQ bulk traffic (ACP 142 is the example).
'Station' and 'node' mean the same thing.
A collision is two or more nodes transmitting at once, or with overlap, so that the signals stop another node receiving.
Listen-before-transmit is what a node does to make sure the channel is free before it tries to transmit.
DCD is the data-carrier-detect signal from the communications equipment interface: true means a carrier is present, false (written !DCD) means the channel is idle.
DCD may not show clearly when a transmission ends, because of fades, and it needs an interface from modem to STANAG 5066 (possibly a crypto bypass).

What DCD is for us: K.2.3 expects DCD on declaration of valid data, some interleaver frames into a transmission. Ours is the demodulator's carrier detect, true from preamble detection to burst end, which is earlier and so more cautious. Reading: that signal is Annex K's DCD.
VDCD is a virtual data-carrier-detect derived from receiving valid D_PDUs.
The EOT field of received D_PDU headers must be used to project forward and predict when the channel will become idle.
notes: Annex K cites C.3.2.3 from the older numbering; in Ed4 the EOT field is C.4.2.3 [p.C-13]. Annex C also requires combining all parsed EOTs and never transmitting before the end time [Ed4 C.7.5.1.1, p.C-110; C.7.5.4.3, p.C-114]; plan 7.2.

requirement: EOT-based end detection is robust, is preferred to DCD and, when available, allows faster switching.
The contention interval is the window in which nodes compete to get onto the shared channel.
Collision avoidance is how contending nodes behave in the contention interval so that, with good odds, one of them gets the channel.
State OFFLINE: the node acts as though it were switched off: no transmitting and no receiving.
State SENSE: the node watches DCD or VDCD until the channel goes quiet.
State LBT_WAIT: on a quiet channel, the node holds off to see whether some other node starts transmitting.
State CONT_WAIT: the node waits a random time before it may transmit, still sensing the channel.
notes: Slotted mode computes a fixed wait instead (K.3.2.3).

requirement: State LINKING: the node may transmit data.
notes: Figure K-1 labels it CAS LINKING; see K-0095.

requirement: Timer LBT_WAIT_TIMER bounds how long a node waits on an idle channel before moving to contention; its value depends on several parameters.
Timer CONT_WAIT_TIMER sets how long a contending node waits before it starts to transmit.
Parameter LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE: the value loaded into LBT_WAIT_TIMER, chosen by the K.3.2.2 rules.
Parameter LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD: the LBT wait used when the end of transmission was found by DCD.
Parameter LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD: the LBT wait used when the end of transmission was found by VDCD.
notes: Default 3 s (K-0103). The text calls the timer 'LBT_WAIT_TIMER_GC' here, a typo for LBT_WAIT_TIMER.

requirement: Parameter CONT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE: computed from other parameters and from whether jitter or slotted is in use.
Parameter NUM_CONT_SLOTS: the number of contention slots.
In slotted mode NUM_CONT_SLOTS must be at least the number of nodes on the network.
notes: Deployment rule; Table 7 says it should equal the node count (K-0100).

requirement: Parameter CONT_SLOT_WIDTH: the duration of each contention slot.
Parameter NODE_SLOT_POSITION: a per-node setting for slotted mode, in the range 1 to NUM_CONT_SLOTS.
In slotted mode every node must be configured with a different NODE_SLOT_POSITION.
notes: Deployment rule; a node can check only its own value against the range.

requirement: Purpose: uncontrolled simultaneous access causes collisions, retransmissions and lost throughput; CSMA with collision avoidance lets a small number of nodes share one frequency.
From offline a node starts in carrier sense. Carrier-sense methods may vary, but Annex K assumes either DCD from the equipment or VDCD from tracking the EOT fields of D_PDUs received earlier.
A node with nothing queued stays in carrier sense.

With data queued and the channel idle, a node enters listen-before-transmit and starts LBT_WAIT_TIMER; the timer restarts whenever carrier is detected, so on a busy channel the wait can be much longer than the timer value.
The LBT wait exists because busy detection is not instantaneous: propagation delay, the modem needing several interleaver frames before declaring DCD, and any delay from relaying DCD through crypto.
When LBT_WAIT_TIMER expires with data still queued the node enters contention, using either the jitter or the slotted mechanism.
In both mechanisms the contention wait is quantised into slots of fixed width, chosen so every node can detect a transmission before the next slot begins.
CONT_SLOT_WIDTH must be greater than the total channel-sensing delay (modem, crypto, propagation and other delays).
notes: Plan 7.2: for us radio TX-to-RX turnaround plus preamble (about 0.72 s) plus audio latency; measured on the bench before changing the default.

requirement: Jitter: the node picks a random slot in which to start transmitting; the random wait spreads out access attempts that carrier sense and LBT tend to synchronise.
With a good slot width, collision probability falls to the chance that two or more contenders pick the same slot; attempts start only on slot boundaries.
Slotted: each node has its own slot and the number of slots equals the number of nodes, so no two nodes pick the same slot and small networks can use few slots.
Slotted needs more coordinated configuration than jitter, is inefficient for large networks, and favours nodes with earlier slots, which shows under high load (where WTRP may suit better).
Informative note: two-node networks need no contention slots, thanks to a later mechanism (the two-node optimisation).
notes: Conflicts with the normative rules; see K-0109 (D7).

requirement: Annex K targets lightly loaded networks where active traffic is often between one pair of nodes, and lets a node transmit at the earliest safe point when it knows only that pair is communicating.

Either node of the active pair may bring in a third node at any time by setting up a CAS-1 link; the optimisation blocks other nodes until the pair finishes, which is accepted for lightly loaded networks.
The protocol is specified by an overall state diagram (K.3.1) and by per-state outbound transition tables (K.3.2).
Figure K-1 shows only states and transition events; the per-state tables of K.3.2 hold the detail.
notes: Figure K-1 shows the LINKING exit only on TX_BUFFER_EMPTY; Table 5 adds the transmit-time limit (K-0093).

requirement: Figure only: a STOP event in any state returns the node to OFFLINE.
notes: Not in any K.3.2 table; the source of STOP is NOT STATED. By symmetry with START we take it from subnetwork management.

requirement: Transitions out of each state must follow that state's outbound transition table, which gives the current state, triggering event, action, next state and any timer started.
A node in OFFLINE neither sends nor receives data.
Transitions out of OFFLINE follow Table 1.
On a START signal from the subnetwork management function (the node starting to operate) the node moves from OFFLINE to SENSE, starting no timer.
In SENSE the node listens for the channel to go idle; idle is the !DCD condition.
Transitions out of SENSE follow Table 2.
A node with no data queued stays in SENSE whatever the channel activity.
A node with data queued waits in SENSE until it detects an idle channel, then moves to LBT_WAIT and starts LBT_WAIT_TIMER.
notes: Table 2. What counts as queued: K-0096.

requirement: LBT rule 1: if the node concludes that the only CAS-1 link in progress is between itself and one other node, LBT_WAIT_TIMER gets the value zero.

Two-node condition (a), which must be checked: the received transmission contains D_PDUs addressed directly to this node and none addressed directly to other nodes; non-ARQ D_PDUs to broadcast or multicast addresses may also be present.

Two-node condition (b), which may be checked: a transmission was received but no D_PDU in it could be parsed, and this node is a peer in every known CAS-1 link on the channel; this needs tracking of all CAS-1 links on the channel, not only this node's own.
LBT rule 2: if DCD (not VDCD) produced the !DCD, LBT_WAIT_TIMER gets LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD.
LBT rule 3: if VDCD (an EOT) produced the !DCD, LBT_WAIT_TIMER gets LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD.
notes: Text misspells the name as LBT_WATI_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD. K-0073.

requirement: Which transmission condition (a) examines, and the order of the rules, are NOT STATED. Reading: rules are tried in the order 1, 2, 3. Condition (a) is evaluated over the D_PDUs parsed from the most recent received transmission, the one whose end produced the !DCD. 'Directly addressed' means an individual (non-group) destination address.

Combining DCD and VDCD: Annex K declares idle on !DCD but treats both DCD and VDCD as busy, and Annex C forbids transmitting before the EOT end time. Reading: the channel is busy while DCD (including any external busy input) is true or a predicted EOT end time lies in the future; !DCD is the moment both have cleared. The !DCD counts as determined by VDCD when the EOT prediction was the last of the two to clear (a tie counts as VDCD), and as determined by DCD otherwise, including when no EOT was parsed.
notes: Ed4 C.7.5.1.1, p.C-110. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: After this node's own transmission (LINKING back to SENSE) neither rule 2 nor rule 3 obviously applies (NOT STATED). Reading: treat the end of our own transmission as determined by VDCD, since the node knows exactly when it ended, so LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD applies; that also gives a peer that answers at once time to be heard, as Table 7 intends.
notes: Ed4 K.4 Table 7, p.K-12. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: A node in LBT_WAIT waits while still sensing channel activity, to make sure the channel really is idle.
Transitions out of LBT_WAIT follow Table 3.
In LBT_WAIT, any busy indication (DCD or VDCD) restarts LBT_WAIT_TIMER with LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD, and the node stays in LBT_WAIT.
In LBT_WAIT, an empty transmit queue (for example emptied by a management function) forces a move to SENSE.
When LBT_WAIT_TIMER expires with data still queued, the node computes CONT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE, starts CONT_WAIT_TIMER and moves to CONT_WAIT.
notes: Table 3. The move to CONT_WAIT is unconditional, even under LBT rule 1; K-0109.

requirement: Jitter: CONT_WAIT_TIMER is CONT_SLOT_WIDTH times a random whole number of slots from 0 to NUM_CONT_SLOTS-1.
Slotted, when the last transmission was not made by this node: CONT_WAIT_TIMER is (NODE_SLOT_POSITION - 1) multiplied by CONT_SLOT_WIDTH.
When the last transmission was made by this node: CONT_WAIT_TIMER is NODE_SLOT_POSITION multiplied by CONT_SLOT_WIDTH.
Rationale for the extra slot: after ARQ data another node is expected to transmit next, but after non-ARQ data perhaps not, so a node repeating its own transmissions leaves room for others.

The jitter random number's distribution and type are NOT STATED; 'multiple of CONT_SLOT_WIDTH' and the slot quantisation of K.2.3 and K.2.4 imply an integer. Reading: an integer uniform over 0 to NUM_CONT_SLOTS-1, drawn from the injected PRNG with a generator specified in the conformance spec so C# and C++ draw identical sequences in tests.

Rule 3 uses NODE_SLOT_POSITION, which exists only in slotted mode, and the text does not say whether it applies to jitter (NOT STATED). Reading: rule 3 is part of the slotted rules; jitter always uses the jitter rule.
notes: NODE_SLOT_POSITION is defined for slotted only [Ed4 K.2.2.10, p.K-4]. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: 'Last transmission' is NOT STATED. Reading: the most recent transmission on the channel, this node's own or one heard (any DCD or VDCD busy period), as of the moment LBT_WAIT_TIMER expires. It was made by this node if no busy period has been seen since this node's own last transmission ended.

LBT_WAIT_TIMER restart: the timer is 'restarted whenever the carrier is detected'. Reading: while the channel is busy the timer is held at its restart value and counts down only once the channel is idle again, so it expires that value after the last busy indication clears. The restart value is LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD as written, even when the new busy period later ends by EOT; its cost in multi-node use is measured in T3/T4 before any change.
notes: Ed4 K.2.3, p.K-5. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Transitions out of CONT_WAIT follow Table 4.

A busy indication in CONT_WAIT means the node lost the contention round: with data still queued it restarts LBT_WAIT_TIMER with the DCD value and returns to LBT_WAIT to wait again for an idle channel.
notes: Table 4. The text names the value LBT_WAIT_TIMER_DCD, read as LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD. Busy includes VDCD (K-0073).

requirement: If CONT_WAIT_TIMER expires while the channel stays idle and data is still queued, the node won the contention round and moves to LINKING, starting no timer.
In CONT_WAIT, an empty transmit queue (for example emptied by a management function) forces a move to SENSE.
Transitions out of LINKING follow Table 5.
A node in LINKING transmits until its transmit buffer is empty or its time transmitting exceeds its maximum transmit interval, then returns to SENSE, starting no timer.
notes: Table 5; the limit's name is clipped in the PDF (MAX_TRANSMIT_INTE...). Figure K-1 shows only TX_BUFFER_EMPTY.

requirement: The maximum transmit interval may be set by the 127.5 s limit of the EOT field, by the time to send the most unacknowledged D_PDUs the ARQ protocol allows, or by a smaller limit from subnetwork management.

Annex C fixes a single-channel transmission's length when it starts and caps it at 127.5 s. Reading: one visit to LINKING is exactly one transmission, built from the queue up to the smallest of 127.5 s, the ARQ window limit and the configured maximum; the node returns to SENSE when it ends. 'CAS LINKING' does not mean CAS-1 link set-up; CAS-1 C_PDUs are ordinary queued data.
notes: Ed4 C, Single Channel and Transmission Length Choice, p.C-113. Item 5 on that page also forbids a transmit-time limit that would stop a large D_PDU being sent at low speed, so the configured maximum must never be below the time for one maximum-length D_PDU at the speed in use. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: 'Data queued for transmission' is NOT STATED. Reading: anything waiting to go on air counts, including ARQ data, acknowledgements, WARNING and MANAGEMENT D_PDUs, CAS-1 C_PDUs, non-ARQ data and identification hook transmissions.
Table 7 lists the scalar parameters that govern the CSMA protocol.
notes: Table numbering skips from Table 5 to Table 7; no Table 6 appears.

requirement: Default CONT_SLOT_WIDTH is 3 seconds; optimising it means making it a function of modem preamble length, data rate and interleaver length.
Default NUM_CONT_SLOTS is 16 (an integer).
For slotted operation, NUM_CONT_SLOTS should equal the network node count.
notes: K.2.2.10 makes at least the node count a shall (K-0037).

requirement: For jitter, NUM_CONT_SLOTS trades the chance that exactly one node picks the winning slot against delay; the example given is 3 nodes and 16 slots for about 90 percent.
Default LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD is 30 seconds, long because a DCD drop may be premature in fades.
Default LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD is 3 seconds: short, but allowing for EOT errors and long enough for waiting nodes to hear a node that answers immediately.
Table 7 gives no default for NODE_SLOT_POSITION (NOT STATED). Reading: it has no default; slotted mode requires it to be configured and checks it lies in 1 to NUM_CONT_SLOTS.
Ed4 adds new timers and scalars to meet the K.2.1 goals; because all nodes must be configured consistently this causes no interoperability issue.
notes: The heading reads 'Changes since Edition 4' but describes changes since Edition 3.

requirement: A network mixing Ed3 and Ed4 systems must be configured with Ed3 settings only.

The Ed3 settings are NOT STATED in Ed4. Reading, from the K.2.1 list of Ed4 additions: Ed3 settings mean jitter contention, LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_DCD and LBT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE_VDCD set to one common value, and LBT rule 1 (zero wait for two nodes) switched off; with K-0085 jitter already has no own-last-transmission rule. The common LBT value is NOT STATED in Ed4 and is set by the operator.
notes: Not listed in plan 4.4. Whether these are offered as a configuration preset or as separate settings is open for D7 (D6 makes Ed3 interop mandatory).

requirement: Annex K's status changed from Informative (Ed3) to Optional, because its timers affect interoperability; this also aligns it with Annex J.

Two-node contention: the informative text says a two-node network needs no contention slots and that a node may transmit at the earliest safe point [K.2.5, K.2.6, p.K-6], but the normative rules only zero the LBT wait [K.3.2.2 rule 1, p.K-9]; on LBT expiry the node always enters CONT_WAIT and draws a contention wait [K.3.2.3, Table 3, p.K-10]. Reading: the normative CONT_WAIT rule applies as written. Resolution is decision D7: CSMA mode (jitter or slotted) and the slot settings are an operator-selectable, network-wide setting, and the default is chosen after T3/T4 measurement.
notes: Plan 4.1, 4.4, 7.2; D7. Also Ed4 J.3.1, p.J-3 (only some simplification is possible for two nodes) and Ed4 K.2.1 addition 2, p.K-2 (two-node switching optimised). With the defaults, jitter averages 22.5 s per turn; in slotted mode the node in position 1 waits zero slots.

requirement: Both contention mechanisms apply: jitter and slotted are both implemented, chosen by the operator as one network-wide setting (D7). Slots are counted from the end of the last transmission, so no shared clock or GPS is needed.
